wiki_article: **OKF Summarization-Governance Proposal** is a working paper by Lee Sharks dated 14 June 2026. This is the second of two records preserving the proposal, recovered from a **Zenodo tombstone `citation_text` capture** — the thinnest recovery tier the archive uses, in which the only surviving evidence is the citation string the repository left behind after deletion. No live authorial surface passed the body-head gate at restoration time, and the captured fields are rendered verbatim. The companion at **#1402** preserves the same proposal from a fuller DataCite capture. Holding both is deliberate: they are two distinct recovery events against the same lost work, and collapsing them would erase the difference between what a full metadata capture preserves and what a tombstone does — a distinction the archive's erosion research exists to measure. The record was held as a metadata capture until 8 August 2026, when the canonical text was recovered from the authorial blog surface and seated as the body.

record_modifications.note: RESTORED from the authorial blog. the record's title names three fields — provenance_kernel, disambiguation, summary_policy — and the post is the GitHub issue proposing exactly those three. Nominated by the new blog index and confirmed by reading; the record had stood as a metadata capture since its mint.

STATE ASSERTION CORRECTED: the article told a reader in the present tense that this record is a metadata capture, while the recovered work sits below it on the same page. The claim was true when written and became false when the text arrived. Rewritten to past tense with the recovery dated; nothing about the work's reading changed.

DESCRIPTION REPLACED: the field carried the capture's provenance prose — source tier, severed DOI, Zenodo removal forensics — which describes how the record was made rather than what the work says. Replaced with the work's own opening and the recovery provenance; prior text retained.

STALE AVAILABILITY CLAIM REMOVED: the field asserted 'This record is a metadata capture; the complete work is not seated here' — a sentence that rendered into the page's META DESCRIPTION, which is the layer search engines and summarizers read. So a record holding its full work was telling every crawler the work was absent.
